title: Finite-cutoff partition comparison envelope and norm-volume pressure diagnostic
question: What cutoff dependence is forced by the unchanged R-464 sextic comparison when its finite-dimensional radial integral is used as an explicit upper envelope?
method: Keep the existing A1/A6/A7 fixed-floor functional, T-054 forward owner order, T-059/T-061 observation-first inverse locks, and all promotion firewalls unchanged.
Reuse the R-464 lower comparison F_N(z)>=a_N||z||^6-K with m=(2N+1)^3 and d=6m, without substituting a proxy for the correlated field law.
Evaluate the standard finite-dimensional radial exp(-beta*a_N*||z||^6) integral in log form for the declared cutoff and beta audit fixtures.
Verify the exact identity a_N*m^3=gamma*V/12 and strict coefficient decrease, then report the induced norm-volume pressure term as a diagnostic only.
Run separate primary, non-importing independent, hostile mutation, integrated, and Lean lanes; issue no intermediate PDF.
decision_scope: T0 finite comparison-envelope and coefficient-scaling diagnostic; no actual partition asymptotic, entropy density, branch probability, tightness, continuum, physical branch, QFT, Yang--Mills, or mass-gap inference
finding: The R-464 lower comparison yields a finite radial upper envelope at each declared finite cutoff and beta. Its coefficient is exactly (gamma*V/12)m^-3 and decreases strictly with cutoff; the resulting positive norm-volume pressure term exposes the boundary of this comparison. The rows do not establish the correlated partition, entropy density, a branch tube, or any limit.
decision_reason: R-465 is the next nonredundant finite diagnostic named by the R-464 boundary. It quantifies the existing comparison before a source-owned correlated Gibbs/tube packet arrives, while preserving the established research methods, owner order, and promotion firewalls.
boundary: The radial expression is an upper envelope from R-464, not the actual correlated full-field partition. The m-dependent pressure term is not an entropy density or a no-go theorem. No cutoff-uniform estimate, branch probability, entropy control, tightness, floor removal, ordered limit, continuum, physical branch, Pre-A, Sector A, QFT, Yang--Mills, or mass-gap result follows.
evidence_level: T0 finite comparison-envelope and coefficient-scaling diagnostic
assumptions: The R-464 sextic lower comparison holds at every fixed cutoff in scope.
The standard finite-dimensional radial integral is used only as a comparison upper envelope.
The cutoff and beta arrays are declared audit fixtures and are not fitted parameters.
missing_assumptions: The actual correlated full-field partition function and its uniform asymptotics.
A source-owned positive-mass active-branch tube, probability, entropy and Jacobian estimate.
A cutoff/volume-uniform compensator, tightness, floor removal and ordered continuum limit.
